description: Implement a real 3-state (closed/open/half-open) circuit breaker in place of a stub that always calls through
prompts: breaker.rb's CircuitBreaker#call(now, &block) always just calls the block. Implement the real 3-state machine: CircuitBreaker.new(failure_threshold, reset_timeout). Starts :closed. In :closed, call invokes the block; if it raises, count consecutive failures, and once `failure_threshold` CONSECUTIVE failures have happened, trip to :open (recording when it opened) and re-raise. While :open, call must NOT invoke the block at all and must instead raise CircuitOpenError - UNLESS at least `reset_timeout` seconds have passed since it opened, in which case it moves to :half_open and allows exactly ONE trial call: if that call succeeds, go back to :closed (reset the failure count); if it raises, go back to :open and RESET the open-time to `now` (so the next trial is only allowed after another full reset_timeout, not immediately). Define CircuitOpenError as a StandardError subclass in the same file.
name: add_ruby_circuit_breaker_state_machine
